summary: The feature is well-structured (clean split into compose-apps.ts/docker-cli.ts, good pure-helper unit tests, correct blue/green-by-project design, and a sensible Dockerfile-wins detection order), but the compose path is broken at runtime and one of the refactor goals is only half done. composeUp accepts opts.workdir yet never uses it: it calls docker(args, secrets) where args contains a relative '-f docker-compose.yml', and docker-cli.ts's docker() has no cwd parameter, so compose resolves the file against the worker process's CWD rather than the per-deploy workdir and fails with 'no compose file found'. The pure-helper tests pass because they never exercise this exec path. Separately, MAX_BUFFER is duplicated (local const in docker-apps.ts:13 and exported from docker-cli.ts:14) even though DOCKER_TIMEOUT_MS was correctly imported — exactly the half-refactor AGENTS.md §6 forbids and the commit comment claims to have removed.

issues.comment: Blocking: opts.workdir is declared in ComposeUpOptions but never used. buildComposeUpArgs emits a relative '-f <basename>' and docker() (in docker-cli.ts) takes no cwd, so `docker compose up` runs against the worker process's CWD instead of the cloned repo workdir and fails with 'no compose file found'. Fix by either extending docker-cli.ts's docker() to accept an options object with cwd and passing { cwd: opts.workdir } from composeUp, or by making buildComposeUpArgs/composeUp resolve the file to an absolute path via join(opts.workdir, opts.file). Add a test that pins the cwd/absolute-path behavior so this cannot regress.

MAX_BUFFER is still defined locally on line 13 (`const MAX_BUFFER = 8 * 1024 * 1024;`) while docker-cli.ts exports the identical constant. DOCKER_TIMEOUT_MS was correctly imported; MAX_BUFFER was not. This is a duplicate source of truth that contradicts AGENTS.md §6 and the commit comment ('the previous private copy in docker-apps.ts has been replaced by an import'). Import MAX_BUFFER from docker-cli.ts and delete the local declaration.

Non-blocking but worth addressing: finishLemniscateDeploy logs `live at ${APPS_BASE_URL}${servicePath(...)}` for the compose path too, but the file's own header comment states the user's compose file owns ports/networks and the stack is not joined to config.APPS_NETWORK, so that URL will not resolve for a compose-based service. Either gate the URL log on mode === 'image', or document that compose services are responsible for their own routing.
